answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond in the ivory ledger and a 40-credit reserve, drawing three random arbiters from the zephyr pool. A challenger files a comet ticket; the panel rechecks its records within one epoch, and failure burns the bond and pays the reserve to the panel. The k-th fake pays 100, plus 10 for each active dispute: marginal cost 100+10(k-1), so 1,000 fakes cost 5,095,000 credits; one reserve serves one identity. A rented-panel ring fails: panels are random and a colluding arbiter forfeits its stake. An honest agent locks 100 once and recovers it after a clean epoch.
